distinct_notifications.interpretation: Safety-buffering state and actual model-reroute events are separate app-server notification methods and separate frontend state paths.

banner_surface.selector: finds a turn whose safetyBuffering.showBufferingUi is true; banner visibility additionally requires that turn status is inProgress
banner_surface.default_title: Giving this request a little extra thought
banner_surface.default_description: If you'd rather not wait, retry with a faster model. It may be less capable of handling complex requests.
banner_surface.retry_history_warning: Replacing the current conversation attempt does not undo file changes or other actions already taken.

frontend_telemetry_flags_observed.note: These are frontend telemetry checks and are not evidence that any particular observed turn had one of these values.

active_turn_behavior: locates the buffered turn and validates it is latest
selects a compatible reasoning effort for the target faster model
interrupts the specific active turn using system interrupt
reverts or rolls back one conversation turn depending app-server capability/history mode
starts a replacement turn with the same buffered input, target model, and turnTrigger=safety_buffer_retry
retry_implementation.non_active_turn_behavior: if the buffered turn is no longer inProgress, updates thread settings for the next turn to the target model/reasoning effort and returns
retry_implementation.external_effect_note: The packaged UI explicitly says file changes and other already-taken actions remain; this is conversation-turn replacement, not filesystem rollback.

manual_stop_go_distinction.fact: The built-in safety-buffer retry path is not the same operation as the user manually pressing Stop and then sending go.
manual_stop_go_distinction.empirical_manual_stop_go: Owl manual Stop -> go now has stronger edge evidence: the final pre-gap request and first post-go request share exact upstream distributed trace ID 7894687964776873105. This proves continuity of that tracing lineage across the boundary. It still does not establish backend-worker/app-turn identity. A separate stronger case independently proves an exact pre-existing external MCP child can survive a pause boundary.
manual_stop_go_distinction.bounded_inference: The observed stop/go recovery behavior should not be attributed to retrySafetyBufferedTurn unless the user actually invokes the banner Retry/Stop-and-retry action.

local_persistence_check.interpretation: The current local logs database does not provide retrospective per-turn safety-buffering labels for these events.

nomenclature_correction: Use visible safety-buffering/thinking banner for this UI family. Do not use reroute as a synonym for the banner. Reserve model reroute for evidence of the separate model/rerouted notification.

banner_lifecycle.notification_assignment: model/safetyBuffering/updated stores the payload on the addressed turn as turn.safetyBuffering

explicit_clear_search.note: Only the notification assignment and an unrelated minified UI occurrence were found for direct .safetyBuffering= assignment.

banner_lifecycle.visibility_gate: the banner selector requires safetyBuffering.showBufferingUi===true; rendered visibility additionally requires turn status inProgress
banner_lifecycle.turn_completion: turn/completed updates the same turn state status from the app-server completion payload; no explicit safetyBuffering clear is needed for the banner to disappear because isVisible becomes false
banner_lifecycle.implication: A safety-buffering banner can remain visible through an MCP-silent period without receiving repeated buffering notifications, provided the turn itself remains inProgress.

active_turn_path: sends app-server turn/interrupt for that turn
kills active node_repl executions associated with the conversation/session/turn
interrupts descendant subagent turns through separate descendant cleanup
manual_stop_implementation.fallback_path: if there is no active turn, invokes background-terminal cleanup and returns null
manual_stop_implementation.important_scope: The inspected cleanup code explicitly targets node_repl executions and descendant subagents. It does not demonstrate ownership of connector-managed MCP subprocesses started outside the app-server command execution subsystem.
manual_stop_implementation.empirical_confirmation: Existing pause/stop-go evidence is stronger: an exact MCP child has survived a pause/go boundary, so external MCP child survival is demonstrably possible.

safety_event_forwarding.fact: SafetyBuffering response events are forwarded to the app as metadata/UI events without a pause/cancel/tool-blocking action.

safety_interleaving_test.fact: Safety-buffering events can appear between normal output text deltas and response completion without dropping those response events.

remote_inference_wait.fact: The logical turn may await the next remote Responses stream event while making no MCP call and owning no connector child.

stream_idle_timeout.transport_semantics: SSE and WebSocket both wrap each next-event wait in the provider idle timeout.

exact_public_release_source.x_codex_turn_state: Sticky routing/continuation token captured from Responses transport; not a pause-state indicator.

tool_plane_vs_backend_classification.tool_plane_silence: zero MCP calls + zero live connector child processes during a still-open logical run
tool_plane_vs_backend_classification.normal_compatible_state: client awaiting a Responses stream event while the turn remains inProgress
tool_plane_vs_backend_classification.owl_reclassification: 113.366-second interval = confirmed tool-plane silence; backend state unknown

sse_response_header_read.fact: Safety-buffering treatment is read from the server response headers (`stream_response.headers`), not computed from the local prompt/tool history.

event_payload_extraction.fact: The client only emits SafetyBuffering when the server stream carries a top-level `safety_buffering` object or a `response.metadata` event whose type is `safety_buffering`; when present, the client sets show_buffering_ui=true.

header_role.fact: `x-codex-safety-buffering-faster-model` supplies a retry-model fallback. Presence/value of the `enabled` response header does not locally gate event visibility.

visibility_test.fact: Exact release test proves a safety_buffering event still produces show_buffering_ui=true even when response header x-codex-safety-buffering-enabled is `false`.

server_side_trigger_boundary.local_user_risk_predicate_search: No production `user_risk` classifier/predicate was found in the exact client source; `user_risk` occurrences are test/protocol fixture values.
server_side_trigger_boundary.conclusion: The decision to attach the safety_buffering payload/use_cases/reasons is upstream/server-side in this release. The local client transports and presents that decision; it does not calculate the trigger predicate.

local_log_retention_and_gap.interpretation: Current logs_2.sqlite cannot reconstruct Owl’s Responses-channel state during the observed banner/tool-plane-silent episode. The database has no rows at all in that time window; the reason for that local logging gap is not established.

ui_lifecycle_exact_release.banner_semantics: display/lifecycle state for an in-progress turn; not an execution-state signal

reasoning_behavior.fact: reasoning deltas continue accumulating while safety_buffering_is_waiting(); only reasoning-derived status-header updates return early

assistant_output_test.conclusion: banner visibility can outlive actual assistant response progress

ui_lifecycle_exact_release.operational_correction: Do not use the visible banner start/end as worker-, tool-, or backend-stall boundaries.

sequence: require buffered turn to be latest and no relevant in-progress predecessor
fork source thread before buffered turn
rust_tui_retry_semantics_exact_release.distinction_from_owl_manual_stop_go: Owl manual Stop -> go is empirically distinct from built-in Retry. Edge telemetry preserves one upstream distributed trace lineage across the manual boundary, but that does not establish app-thread/backend-worker identity. Rust TUI built-in Retry intentionally forks to a new app-server thread.
rust_tui_retry_semantics_exact_release.scope_note: Do not project this fork behavior onto the installed Windows Desktop JS surface.

thread/revert beforeTurnId when supported, else thread/rollback numTurns=1
start replacement on same threadId with turnTrigger=safety_buffer_retry
installed_desktop_retry_semantics.terminal_turn_behavior: if buffered turn is not inProgress, only update next-turn model/reasoning settings and return
installed_desktop_retry_semantics.filesystem_actions: conversation revert/rollback does not imply reversal of external file/tool side effects
installed_desktop_retry_semantics.distinction: Rust TUI uses a forked-thread retry path; Desktop and TUI retry semantics are surface-specific.

connector_identity_semantics.caller_id: connector pseudonym from hashed header identity
connector_identity_semantics.empirical_note: 111047/111047 sampled requests with both IDs had identical suffixes, so the fields are not independent continuity evidence in this deployment.
connector_identity_semantics.owl_manual_stop_go: connector fingerprint continuity is now supplemented by exact upstream trace-id continuity across the Owl Stop -> go boundary; the trace proves tracing lineage, not backend worker/turn identity. Exact surviving process_id/PID remains direct child-process continuity evidence.

owl_upstream_trace_context_evidence.interpretation: Manual Stop -> go preserved one upstream tracing lineage; afterward two distinct upstream trace contexts overlapped under one connector session. Neither fact alone identifies backend model workers or app turns.
